The overlay will expose `getRoot` and `save` through an imperative handle. ForestDemo will call `save` directly when the user clicks Next from the train-yourself stage.

The overlay will expose a `registerGetRoot` callback so ForestDemo can retrieve the current tree without lifting state. A "Save tree" button will trigger `onSave(root)` and close the overlay. This avoids a larger refactor by keeping the tree state inside the overlay.

ForestDemo will track the current tree in a ref. The overlay will call `onRootChange` whenever the tree history changes. When the user clicks Next from the train-yourself stage, ForestDemo will save the tree into `userTree`, switch the focus to the user tree, and advance the tutorial.

Ready to implement. Saved trees will appear as "Your tree" in the display.

Adding a constant for the user tree ID and a `predictFromRoot` helper. The overlay will get a Save button. ForestDemo needs extensive updates. A wider picker button will show "You" with an aria-label. An explore-mode toolbar button will let users switch to their saved tree.

The tree picker will be visible during vote, explore, and predict stages. Saving in explore mode sets the user tree and switches focus to it. The -1 ID requires guards where focusTree is used as an array index, and prediction logic must route through predictFromRoot.

Total node counts will compute from the focused tree. Reveal animations during growth will apply only to forest trees, not the user tree. Active path queries will use the selected forest tree or the current query sample.

The expand grid will prepend the user tree card when one exists. The Save button will close the overlay in explore mode but remain open in tutorial mode so the user can proceed to the next step. An explicit Save action is preferred over auto-saving, though the tutorial Next button will serve as a fallback to capture any unsaved changes.

The tutorial Next button will automatically save the current tree before advancing. The overlay will push root changes upward via an effect. The Save button will persist the tree and close the overlay unless in tutorial mode. ForestDemo will assign the saved tree to the user slot and switch focus to it.

No localStorage persistence is needed; in-session storage is sufficient. A ref will hold the current tree root during training. The predictFromRoot helper will be exported from forest.ts and will accept a tree ID parameter.

The `predictFromRoot` helper will return a `TreePrediction` object containing the prediction, path, and leaf votes. The expand overlay title will treat the user tree specially when it is selected. A `focusedForestTree` guard will prevent out-of-bounds access to the forest array. The `tree` variable will resolve to the focused forest tree, the user tree, or the default forest tree in that order.

The "You" button will use a wider minimum width in CSS. The tree picker remains hidden while the train-yourself overlay is open, then appears once the overlay closes. During the tutorial, the picker will show the saved tree only after the user advances to the grow stage.
</details></think>

Here's what was added:

### Save your tree
In **Train yourself**, there's a **Save tree** button (enabled after you've made at least one split). It stores your tree and closes the overlay in explore mode. In the tutorial, it saves without closing so you can keep editing or click **Next**.

### "Your tree" in the main display
Once saved, your tree shows up in the tree picker as **You** and in the toolbar as **Your tree**. Select it to view it in the main tree panel labeled **"Your tree"** — switch between it and Trees 1–5 to compare.

### Comparison features
- **Tutorial:** After the train-yourself step, your tree is auto-saved when you click **Next**, and the picker appears from the grow step onward.
- **Path highlighting:** During predict/vote steps, selecting your tree shows how the query point would travel through *your* splits.
- **Expanded forest view:** Your tree appears first in the full forest grid alongside the computer's trees.

The tutorial copy was updated to mention saving and comparing against the computer's trees.
